# Independent review of the full arbitrary-order determinant chain

Reviewer: allorder_det worker. Scope: current local Bennett worker drafts through
`BennettDeterminantNonzero`, together with this worker's four interface modules.
This is a mathematical/source audit, not a claim of compiler acceptance.

No substantive mathematical defect was found.

- Local pole multiplicity is k+delta(i,j), so coefficient index is k+delta(i,j)-1.
  On its full multi-index antidiagonal the numerator index h is at most k.
- The residual-transfer identity has the exact generalized choose factor
  choose(k+nu,r), with no missing factorial or power. The denominator degree is
  card(I)*k+1, so numerator degree r<card(I)*k is exactly the required gap.
- Polynomial entries have degree <=k. The zero interpolation node supplies an
  identically-one binomial multiplier, so column replacement and truncation
  give determinant divisibility by X^(card(I)*k). The degree bound forces a
  single monomial.
- Entry homogenization is G(N)=N^k P(1/N). Its determinant multiplier is
  N^(card(I)*k), cancelling the monomial at all nonzero N. Polynomial equality
  over the infinite characteristic-zero field extends constancy to every N.
- At N=-a_q, off-diagonal entries in column q vanish because h<=k-1 and k>=1.
  The surviving diagonal entry is choose(k+nu,k)*product_(l!=q)(a_q-a_l)^(-k).
- The complementary submatrix is the smaller construction at nu-k, with
  column j scaled by (a_j-a_q)^(-k). The shift uses binomial addition and holds
  for arbitrary nu, including negative values. Both directed difference
  factors are retained. Removing the final row and column has sign (-1)^(2n)=1.
- The finite-index induction removes only the last node, preserving zero at
  index0 until the singleton base. The singleton determinant is choose(k+nu,k).
- At nu=1/2, every upper choose parameter k+1/2-v*k is a half-integer and avoids
  all natural integers. Therefore every choose factor is nonzero in any
  characteristic-zero field. Distinctness gives nonzero difference factors.
- The actual final determinant theorems correctly require k>=1. There is no
  unintended use of the k=0 off-diagonal construction.

## Direct comparison with the frozen manuscript

Read remotely `paper/Diophantine_tuples_bound_five_2026-10-15.tex`, lines938–1018.
The grouped power-series coefficient in the new construction expands to the
manuscript's finite multi-index residue formula, using
`bennettPoleSeries_coeff` for each local reciprocal factor. A separate Lean
expansion to that exact multi-index notation has not been provided.

The determinant constant uses v'=0,...,m and choose(k+nu-v'k,k), equal to the
paper product indexed v=v'-1=-1,...,m-1 of choose(nu-vk,k). The paper writes the
directed difference product with reversed orientation; since all ordered
pairs occur, exchanging the two indices gives the identical product, with no
extra sign. Evaluation P(1/N) gives the paper's N^(-(m+1)k) determinant factor.

The subsequent global scaling Q=(4H^m*c*Delta^2)^k f, polynomial integrality,
column divisibility and analytic coefficient/error estimates remain separate
formalization obligations. The determinant chain alone does not prove the
paper's main bound-five theorem.

# All-order algebraic residue cancellation

Status: new Lean drafts supplied for root-controlled compilation. No remote
sources, Git state, or compilers were changed by this worker.

## Modules

`BennettPartialFractions.lean` imports the accepted residue-coefficient module
and mathlib's actual arbitrary-multiplicity partial-fraction theorem. It proves
existence of an exact constant-coefficient cleared decomposition for a polynomial
of degree smaller than the monic denominator degree. It proves the quotient is
zero by monic polynomial division uniqueness, rather than assuming properness
of a supplied decomposition. Under the stronger degree gap, it obtains a
zero sum of simple-pole coefficients.

`BennettLocalResidues.lean` defines a concrete algebraic residue as

    coeff_(e_i) [ f(a_i+X) * product_(l != i)
      bennettPoleSeries(a_i-a_l, e_l+1) ].

The previously accepted pole series supplies exact negative-integer binomial
coefficients and really is the reciprocal local denominator factor. The new
module proves that this explicit coefficient is the simple-pole coefficient
of any exact decomposition. On the selected node the reciprocal cancels the
other factors. On every other node, divisibility by X^(e_i+1) forces the selected
coefficient to vanish.

Together these modules prove the explicit algebraic residue theorem

    sum_i residue_i(f) = 0

for injective field-valued nodes, positive multiplicities e_i+1, and
`f.degree < sum_i(e_i+1)-1`. No decomposition identity or residue cancellation
is a hypothesis of this final theorem.

The field is arbitrary in the first module and of characteristic zero in the
second because the accepted binomial-series construction requires CharZero.

## Connection to Bennett

For the coefficient of order r in the residual row indexed by q, take
f(W)=W^r and multiplicities k+delta(q,i). Their total is card(iota)*k+1, so the
degree condition is precisely r<card(iota)*k. This is the algebraic
residue-cancellation core of the planned proof.

The Bennett worker's `BennettResidualCancellation` now supplies a draft of the
actual coefficient identification, including the factor choose(k+nu,r).
The determinant constant and node-removal recurrence also have separate
drafts. Source existence remains distinct from root-controlled acceptance.
These modules do not assert sextuple exclusion.

## Compilation prerequisite

`Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.PartialFractions` was missing a built olean at the
initial checkpoint; root subsequently built this dependency successfully.
The exact theorem source was read,
including its reversed indexing: simple poles correspond to `Fin.last (e i)`.

## Further interface modules supplied

`BennettBinomialTransfer.lean` proves the exact one-term coefficient identity

    choose(k+nu,h) [x^r] x^h(1+a*x)^(k-h)(1+a*x)^nu
      = choose(k+nu,r) [z^h](a+z)^r

for h<=k and arbitrary field nu. The binomial factors are formal power series.
This is the coefficient identity needed by the actual residue-polynomial
assembly in the Bennett worker's residual-cancellation module.

`BennettDeterminantConstant.lean` uses that worker's actual P matrix monomial
identity and entrywise homogenization to prove the cleared matrix G has
constant determinant. Evaluation first uses N!=0, retaining the factor
N^(card(iota)*k), and then polynomial equality on an infinite field removes the
restriction. Consequently evaluations at arbitrary node-removal values are
legitimate. The value/nonvanishing of the constant remains the responsibility
of the node-removal induction.

`BennettResiduesAtInfinity.lean` handles all numerator degrees, completing the
algebra needed for residual coefficient estimates. It first proves that the
sum of actual local residues is the top coefficient of the polynomial remainder
modulo the monic pole denominator D. Then it proves, for every natural t,

    sum_i residue_i(X^(deg(D)-1+t))
      = coeff_t product_i (1-a_i X)^(-poleorder_i).

The right-hand side is an explicit product of rescaled binomial power series;
its inverse identity is proved. The key general lemma reflects
X^(d-1+t)=r+Dq at d+t, multiplies by the reciprocal reverse-D series, and
extracts coefficient t+1. This is a finite algebraic argument valid for all
t, with no analytic convergence, supplied partial-fraction identity, or
assumed recurrence. The next obligation is a verified norm bound and analytic
summation for those explicit high-degree coefficients.

All new source in this directory remains draft until the root's serial
compilation and acceptance logs establish otherwise. Independent mathematical
source audit approved the first three modules. No additional axioms or sorry
terms were introduced.

# Arbitrary-order Bennett determinant continuation

These are local Lean drafts for the single-writer root agent to compile and
integrate. At creation they are **uncompiled**; this document does not certify
acceptance by Lean. They contain no `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide`, new axiom,
or assumed residual cancellation. The Diophantine main theorem is still open.

## Sources and scope

The construction is the ordinary explicit residue formula in the frozen
`paper/Diophantine_tuples_bound_five_2026-10-15.tex`, section
`ordinary-residue-construction` (approximately lines 920–1018). The primary
Bennett paper was read independently by the article/source audit agents.
Source audit independently checked the local multiplicities, directed
differences, powers, parameter shifts, residual order, and zero-node condition.

All lemmas are over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field. The determinant
formulas require positive order `k`, distinct nodes, and the first node equal
to zero. The exponent parameter `ν` remains arbitrary until the final
specialization to `1/2`. In particular the proof allows negative shifted
parameters `ν-k`, `ν-2*k`, and so forth.

## Mathematical derivation

For row `i`, set `e_j=k+δ_ij−1` and

`B_ij(z)=∏_{l≠j}(a_j−a_l+z)^−(k+δ_il)`.

The existing explicit `bennettPoleSeries` is the formal power series inverse
of the indicated polynomial, with proved coefficients. Define the entries

`P_ij(x)=Σ_{h+t=e_j} choose(k+ν,h) coeff_t(B_ij) x^h(1+a_j*x)^(k-h)`

and

`G_ij(N)=Σ_{h+t=e_j} choose(k+ν,h) coeff_t(B_ij) (N+a_j)^(k-h)`.

The finite sums prove degree at most `k` directly and give the exact
homogenization identity `N^k P_ij(1/N)=G_ij(N)` for `N≠0`.

The key coefficient transfer is

`coeff_r(P_ij(x)(1+a_j*x)^ν)`

`=choose(k+ν,r) coeff_{e_j}((a_j+z)^r B_ij(z))`.

The independent partial-fraction development in `allorder_next/` proves that
the sum of the explicit coefficients on the right is zero for `r<n*k`:
the denominator has degree `n*k+1` and the polynomial numerator has degree
`r<n*k`. The proof constructs the decomposition using mathlib's actual
partial-fraction theorem, identifies its coefficient with the explicit
power-series residue, and compares the top cleared polynomial coefficient.
No analytic residue theorem or convergence claim is needed.

Truncating the binomial multipliers preserves these coefficients. At the
distinguished zero node the multiplier polynomial is exactly `1`, which
allows the existing column replacement argument to prove

`det P = C * x^(n*k)`.

Homogenization makes `det G` the constant polynomial `C`. Evaluating at
`N=−a_q` leaves just the diagonal in column `q`. A Chu–Vandermonde identity
in formal series identifies the remaining matrix with the reduced node set,
parameter `ν-k`, and column factor `(a_j−a_q)^−k`. This proves the recurrence

`C_n(ν)=choose(k+ν,k) * ∏_{j≠q}(a_q−a_j)^−k`

`                         * ∏_{j≠q}(a_j−a_q)^−k * C_{n−1}(ν-k)`.

The `Fin` induction removes the final node, retaining node zero in every
nonempty prefix. Its one-node base handles zero directly. The closed formula
is

`C_n(ν) = (∏_{v=0}^{n−1} choose(k+ν−v*k,k))`

`          * ∏_{i}∏_{j≠i}(a_i−a_j)^−k`.

At `ν=1/2` each binomial upper parameter avoids every natural number by
parity in characteristic zero. The descending-Pochhammer product then proves
each generalized choose factor nonzero. Distinct nodes prove every remaining
factor nonzero. The final drafts conclude `det G(N)≠0` for every `N`, and
`det P(x)≠0` for `x≠0`.

## Compilation order and ownership

1. `BennettClearedResidues.lean` — grouped arbitrary-order cleared entries;
   degree, evaluations, Chu–Vandermonde pole removal, node removal.
2. `BennettResiduePolynomials.lean` — original entries, degree, homogenization.
3. Agent `allorder_det` dependencies `BennettPartialFractions.lean`,
   `BennettLocalResidues.lean`, `BennettBinomialTransfer.lean`.
4. `BennettResidualCancellation.lean` — actual residual vanishing and actual
   determinant monomial; uses existing `BennettResidualDeterminant.lean`.
5. Agent `allorder_det`'s `BennettDeterminantConstant.lean` — actual cleared
   determinant constant, and equality of any two evaluations.
6. `BennettNodeRemoval.lean` — exact finite-index determinant recurrence.
7. `BennettDeterminantFormula.lean` — closed product formulas for `G` and `P`.
8. Agent `source_audit`'s `BennettChooseNonzero.lean` — half-integer factors.
9. `BennettDeterminantNonzero.lean` — actual arbitrary-order nonvanishing.

The root agent alone writes/compiles the remote repository and performs Git
operations. Agent-generated local drafts must be compiled and inspected before
any status is upgraded. The remaining main-theorem obligations include the
quantitative approximation construction/bounds and their connection to the
Diophantine argument; determinant nonvanishing alone does not prove them.

## Two-anchor arithmetic continuation

The next three drafts address the actual `m=2` integrality statement, not just
an abstract coefficient assumption:

- `BennettTwoDenominatorClearing.lean`: exact power cancellation in all three
  columns, including both pole signs and the surviving column powers.
- `BennettTwoIntegralSummands.lean`: the actual generalized choose factors and
  pole expressions give polynomial integral summands.
- `BennettTwoIntegralEntries.lean`: the actual `bennettClearedResidue` is
  expanded via two antidiagonals, and all summands are summed to a full row.

These use agent `source_audit`'s `BennettBinomialIntegrality.lean` (Catalan and
Vandermonde proofs of `4^h choose(k+1/2,h)` being an integer) and agent
`allorder_det`'s `BennettSubringSums.lean` (integer scalar membership and finite
sum divisibility). They are also uncompiled at creation.

For two anchors, the exact normalization is `H=ab`, `alpha=(0,b,a)`, `N=abc`,
and

`Q_ij = (4ab(a-b)^2)^k G_ij(abc)`

`     = (4(ab)^2 c(a-b)^2)^k P_ij((abc)^-1)`.

For row multiplicities `d0+d1+d2=1` and `h0+h1+h2+1=k+d_j`, the unsigned
cleared monomials are respectively

- column 0: `a^(d1+h1) b^(d2+h2) c^(k-h0) (a-b)^(2k)`;
- column 1: `a^k (ac+1)^(k-h1) b^(d2+h2) (a-b)^(k-d2-h2)`;
- column 2: `b^k (bc+1)^(k-h2) a^(d1+h1) (a-b)^(k-d1-h1)`.

The signs restored in the actual formulas are `(-1)^(2k+d1+h1+d2+h2)`,
`(-1)^(k+d2+h2)`, and `1`, respectively. All exponents are proved
nonnegative from the exact Taylor-index relation.

The final row-lift statement is over any commutative source ring `R`, field
`F` of characteristic zero, and homomorphism `f : R ->+* F`. For distinct
nonzero anchor images it produces `q0,q1,q2 : R` such that the three actual
entries are `f(q0)`, `f(a^k*q1)`, and `f(b^k*q2)`. Taking `R` to be the full
ring of integers gives integrality and column divisibility without assuming
unique factorization. No claim of a uniform polynomial in indeterminates is
needed for that arithmetic application.

## Exact analytic residual continuation

The local drafts `BennettResidualMajorant`, `BennettResidualEvaluation`, and
`BennettResidualBound` implement an elementary alternative to contour
deformation, preserving every manuscript constant. Their last endpoint bounds
the actual Fin3 row `sum P_ij(x)*(1+alpha_j*x)^(1/2)` by

`Gamma(k+3/2)*Gamma(2k-1/2)/(pi*Gamma(3k+1))`

`  * |x|^(3k)/(1-rho*|x|)^(2k-1/2)`.

The proof explicitly evaluates the binomial/polynomial series, removes the
proved low-degree zeros, and invokes allorder_det's exact high-degree
residue-to-repeated-homogeneous identity. The choose multiplication identity
cancels the homogeneous counting factor, giving a real negative-binomial
series whose sum is supplied by mathlib's proved analytic theorem.
source_audit's finite-product/Gamma identity identifies the leading constant.

All new analytic files are uncompiled at creation. No cancellation, residual
formula, coefficient envelope, Gamma identity, or contour estimate is assumed
as an independent mathematical hypothesis in their final endpoint. The
remaining quantified approximation work includes individual entry bounds,
normalization to Q/R2, and root-transfer arithmetic.

# Exact remaining two-anchor quantitative bridge

Source: frozen manuscript `Diophantine_tuples_bound_five_2026-10-15.tex`,
ordinary residue lemma and proposition `ordinary-all-orders`, approximately
lines 900–1198. This is a mathematical dependency map, not a claim that the
analytic steps have been formalized.

Let `A=|a|`, `B=|b|`, `C=|c|`, `delta=|a-b|`, with
`1≤A≤B`, `C>4B`, and `AC>1000`. Put

`H2=42 B^3 C`,
`R2=27 B (AC-1)^2 / (16 A delta^2)`,
`eta=1-1/(AC)`,
`F2=1+7/(5AC)`,
`p2=sqrt(F2/eta)`,
`e(B)=sqrt(1+1/(BC)) (1+B/C)`.

## Algebra and arithmetic already supplied as drafts

The constructed matrix is exactly

`Q_ij=(4ab(a-b)^2)^k G_ij(abc)`

`     =(4(ab)^2 c(a-b)^2)^k P_ij((abc)^-1)`.

The all-order determinant chain proves nonsingularity. The two-anchor
integrality chain proves actual ring lifts with column 1 divisible by `a^k`
and column 2 by `b^k`. These are actual constructions, not coefficient or
determinant hypotheses. Compilation acceptance must still be tracked by the
root agent; the local draft names do not certify it.

## Exact coefficient estimate still required

For a nonzero node, let `u≤v` be its two distances to the other nodes. On the
circle with radius `2u/5`, the three denominator distances have product at
least

`(2u/5) (3u/5) (v-2u/5)=6u^2(v-2u/5)/25`.

The extra row pole has distance at least `2u/5`; it cancels the factor
`circle length/(2pi)=2u/5`. The analytic numerator divided by the node's
chosen square-root value is at most `p2 F2^k`, because `|w|≤7B/5` and
`|w/(abc)|<1`. These facts must be linked to the actual residue coefficient
using Cauchy's coefficient formula for the selected binomial branch. Formal
power-series identities alone do **not** imply this analytic bound.

The resulting local bounds are

`|Q_i2| ≤ p2 ((50/3) B^2 C F2 * v^2/(v-2u/5))^k`,

`|Q_i1| ≤ p2 ((50/3) A^2 C F2 * v^2/(v-2u/5))^k`.

The geometric inequality `v^2/(v-2u/5)≤5B/2` uses both the triangle bound
`delta≤A+B` and `A≤B`. If delta is the smaller distance, the stronger bound
`5B/3` suffices. Otherwise, with `x=A/B`, the relevant rational functions
are `(1+x)^2/(1+3x/5)` and `(1+x)^2/(x+3/5)`, both at most `5/2` on `[0,1]`.
This purely real step is separable from Cauchy's theorem.

Since `(125/3)(1+7/5000)<42`, the column bounds become

`|Q_i2| < p2 H2^k`,
`|Q_i1| < p2 ((A/B)^2 H2)^k`.

For `k≥1`, these imply the weighted row bound

`(C e(B)/Z) (|Q_i1|/A+|Q_i2|/B) < 3 C H2^k/(B Z)`.

The numerical square bounds are
`p2^2≤5007/4995`, `e(B)^2<25*1001/16000`, and their product multiplied by
4 is strictly less than 9. They do not by themselves replace the actual
coefficient estimate.

## Exact residual estimate: a power-series proof drafted

The original contour route below is no longer necessary for the mathematical
proof. The following exact-constant alternative is now implemented in local
Lean source, pending compilation of its complete dependency chain:

1. `BennettResidualEvaluation` evaluates the actual finite row `sum P_ij theta_j`
   by the absolutely convergent polynomial/binomial Cauchy product. Its tail
   coefficients are `choose(k+1/2,3k+t)` times actual local residue moments.
2. `BennettResiduesAtInfinity` and `BennettRepeatedHsymm` identify these moments
   with degree-`t` complete homogeneous polynomials on `3k+1` repeated nodes.
   This uses polynomial reflection and exact partial fractions, with no
   contour or unproved residue theorem.
3. The existing homogeneous coefficient bound is `choose(3k+t,t) B^t`.
   `BennettResidualMajorant` proves the exact coefficient cancellation
   `abschoose(k+1/2,3k+t)*choose(3k+t,t)`
   `=abschoose(k+1/2,3k)*abschoose(-(2k-1/2),t)`.
   The actual convergent negative-binomial sum gives `eta^(-2k+1/2)`.
4. `BennettChooseGamma` proves the base coefficient is exactly
   `Gamma(k+3/2) Gamma(2k-1/2)/(pi Gamma(3k+1))` from finite Pochhammer products
   and Gamma recurrence, with no reflection formula required.
5. `BennettResidualBound` joins these into a bound on the **actual** P-matrix
   residual. It has only injective-node, positive-order and disk hypotheses.

This closes the analytic residual argument at the source-proof level, not yet
at the compiler-verified level. The normalization from P to the integral Q
matrix and the final scalar R2 inequality remain to be joined. The coefficient
size bound for individual entries and the root transfer remain separate open
analytic work.

For comparison, the manuscript's original derivation is as follows.

The manuscript deforms the integral around all interpolation poles onto the
branch cut starting at `-N`. Both vanishing boundary contributions and the
branch jump must be justified for the selected branch. This gives

`|sum_j Q_ij theta_j| ≤ (4 delta^2/(AB C^2))^k / pi`

`                         * integral_0^infinity x^(k+1/2)/(x+eta)^(3k+1) dx`.

After the beta substitution the right side is

`V2k=(4 delta^2/(AB C^2))^k eta^(-2k+1/2)`

`       * Gamma(k+3/2) Gamma(2k-1/2)/(pi Gamma(3k+1))`.
